title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 7 — Ratio Practice
question: 48 fresh questions: two for each of the 24 worked Ratio examples.
intro:
- Two fresh questions for every worked example in the Ratio Material.
- Groups follow cards 1–6 and examples a–d.
- For a numerical question, enter only the requested value in the stated unit.
- Use simplest form for fractions and ratios.

questions.prompt:
4 notebooks cost €12.

How much do 7 notebooks cost?
questions.solution:
\[\text{Cost of one notebook}=12\div 4\]

\[\text{One unit}=3\]

\[3\times 7=21\]

\[\boxed{21}\text{ euros}\]

Find one unit first, then multiply by the number needed; both quantities scale together.

questions.prompt: Write \(80\) cm : \(2\) m in simplest form.
questions.solution:
\[2\text{ m}=200\text{ cm}\]

\[80 : 200=80 : 200\]

\[\text{HCF}=40\]

\[80 : 200=\boxed{2 : 5}\]

- Use the same units first; clear decimals if needed, then divide both terms by their HCF.
- Keep the order.

questions.prompt:
Find \(x\), or decide that no solution exists:

\[3:4:7=x:8:14\]
questions.solution:
\[\text{Middle multiplier}=8\div 4\]

\[\text{Middle multiplier}=2\]

\[\text{Last multiplier}=14\div 7\]

\[\text{Last multiplier}=2\]

\[x=3\times 2\]

\[\boxed{6}\]

The known pairs agree, so apply their common multiplier to the missing term.

questions.prompt:
Find \(x\), or decide that no solution exists:

\[3:4:8=x:6:10\]
questions.solution:
\[\text{Middle multiplier}=6\div 4\]

\[\text{Middle multiplier}=\frac{3}{2}\]

\[\text{Last multiplier}=10\div 8\]

\[\text{Last multiplier}=\frac{5}{4}\]

\[\frac{3}{2}\ne \frac{5}{4}\]

\[\boxed{\text{No solution}}\]

- All three terms need one common multiplier.
- A value from just one known pair cannot repair the other pair.

questions.prompt:
Share €60 in the ratio \(2 : 3\).

How many euros are in the first share?
questions.solution:
\[\text{Total parts}=2+3\]

\[\text{Total parts}=5\]

\[\text{One part}=60\div 5\]

\[\text{One part}=12\]

\[\text{First share}=2\times 12\]

\[\boxed{24}\text{ euros}\]

- Add all the ratio parts before dividing the total.
- A ratio does not mean equal shares.

questions.prompt:
A map has scale \(1:20000\).

Two places are \(4\) cm apart on the map.

Find the real distance in m.
questions.solution:
\[\text{Real distance (cm)}=4\times 20000\]

\[\text{Real distance (cm)}=80000\]

\[\text{Real distance (m)}=80000\div 100\]

\[\boxed{800}\text{ m}\]

- The scale compares matching units: 1 cm on the map represents the scale number of centimetres in real life.
- Convert units carefully.
